summary: Defines a two-way mapping for one-to-one chat sessions between SIP and XMPP users. For SIP text chat, it specifies a mapping to the Message Session Relay Protocol. This extends the single-message mapping.

eli5.summary: Like the other translator document, but for whole back-and-forth conversations.

questions: how does sip chat interwork with xmpp
how do xmpp and sip chat sessions map
subtitle: How a gateway turns SIP/MSRP one-to-one chat sessions into XMPP chat messages, and back.

tldr.problem: SIP systems negotiate a formal chat session and carry text over MSRP, while XMPP users just send chat messages with no session setup, so the two cannot talk to each other directly.
tldr.mechanism: A gateway keeps extra state: it opens an MSRP session through a SIP INVITE when an XMPP chat message arrives, maps messages in both directions, and uses the XMPP gone chat state and SIP BYE to end sessions. Composing events, delivery reports and message size limits are mapped too.
tldr.outcome: SIP and XMPP users can hold one-to-one text chats through a gateway. This RFC covers session-mode chat only; single messages and groupchat are in separate documents.

today: RFC 7573 is a Proposed Standard published in June 2015, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It extends the single-message mapping of RFC 7572 to chat sessions.

sections.title: Why Chat Needs State in the Gateway
sections.content:
Both the Session Initiation Protocol (SIP, RFC 3261) and the Extensible Messaging and Presence Protocol (XMPP, RFC 6120) can carry one-to-one text chat. This RFC defines the two-way mapping between XMPP messages of type chat and the Message Session Relay Protocol (MSRP, RFC 4975), which SIP-based systems commonly use for chat. MSRP is not tied to SIP and can be used by non-SIP technologies.

The architecture, address mapping and error handling come from RFC 7247. Single instant messages are covered by RFC 7572, and groupchat by a separate document.

The key difference is that SIP chat sessions are formally negotiated, while an XMPP chat session is informal: a user sends a message of type chat, the contact replies, and the messages exchanged over a period of time count as a session, ideally tied together with an XMPP thread element. So a gateway needs to keep additional state.
sections.eli5: One side asks 'may we talk?' and waits for a yes before chatting. The other side just starts chatting. The gateway has to remember who is in which conversation to bridge the two habits.

sections.title: From XMPP to MSRP
sections.content:
When an XMPP user sends a chat message to someone in a SIP domain, the XMPP server finds the domain type using the procedures in Section 5 of RFC 7247 and hands the stanza to an XMPP-to-SIP gateway. The gateway then starts an MSRP session on the sender's behalf with a SIP INVITE whose SDP offers a message media line and an MSRP path. There is no reliable way to know whether the recipient's client supports MSRP, so session initiation might result in an error.

If the SIP user accepts with a 200 OK, the gateway sends an ACK and then relays the original text as an MSRP SEND. The SIP user's replies come back as MSRP SEND requests and are turned into XMPP chat messages, reusing the same thread identifier. The mapping of syntax itself MUST follow RFC 7572.

When the SIP user ends the session with a BYE, the gateway acknowledges it. XMPP has no formal session end, and RFC 6121 defines no method for an XMPP user to end one, so the gateway has to watch for a gone chat state or use a timer.
sections.eli5: Juliet just starts talking. The gateway politely asks Romeo 'can we chat?' for her, waits for him to say yes, and then passes along what she said and what he says back.

sections.title: From MSRP to XMPP
sections.content:
In the other direction a SIP user sends an INVITE with an MSRP offer. The SIP server decides the target domain is an XMPP domain, using the same procedures from RFC 7247, and hands the invitation to an MSRP-to-XMPP gateway.

The gateway accepts the session with a 200 OK on behalf of the XMPP user, so the XMPP user is never asked. After the ACK, each MSRP SEND becomes an XMPP message of type chat, with the SIP Call-ID used as the thread, and replies from the XMPP user are turned back into MSRP SEND requests. When the SIP user sends BYE, the gateway accepts it on the XMPP user's behalf.
sections.eli5: When Romeo calls first, the gateway says 'yes, she is available' without asking Juliet, then repeats his words to her and hers to him.

sections.title: Composing Events and the Gone State
sections.content:
XMPP Chat State Notifications (XEP-0085) define five states: active, inactive, gone, composing and paused. Indication of Message Composition (RFC 3994) defines two, idle and active. Gateways can map only the composing-related states or all of them, and the suggested mappings are in the table below.

The gone state has no isComposing equivalent, but it has a use: receiving it at an XMPP-to-MSRP gateway can trigger a SIP BYE, and receiving a BYE at an MSRP-to-XMPP gateway can trigger a gone notification to the XMPP user. Gateways that support chat state notifications MUST support gone, which XEP-0085 only recommends. Gateways can also use a timer to trigger gone when the XMPP user is silent, and XEP-0085 suggests an example of 10 minutes.
sections.eli5: When your friend is typing, you see 'typing...'. When they walk away, the gateway can hang up the call for them, or tell them the other side hung up.

sections.title: Delivery Reports and Message Size
sections.content:
XMPP Message Receipts (XEP-0184) and MSRP REPORT requests both tell a sender that a message arrived. An XMPP request element maps to an MSRP Success-Report header with value yes, and a received element maps to an MSRP REPORT request, and the reverse. XMPP receipts do not support failure reports, so there is no mapping for Failure-Report and gateways SHOULD set it to no.

On size, a SIP page-mode MESSAGE request is not allowed to exceed 1300 bytes, but MSRP can break larger messages into several SEND requests, which the gateway must reassemble. In XMPP, the maximum stanza size must not be less than 10,000 bytes (RFC 6120, Section 13.12). Administrators need to configure the MSRP gateway with the same or a smaller maximum message size, which the gateway reports in the SDP max-size attribute. A gateway that receives a message above its limit MUST return an MSRP 413 error.
sections.eli5: Delivery reports are like asking the post office to tell you when your letter arrived. Message size rules keep one huge parcel from jamming the system.

sections.title: Security and Internationalization
sections.content:
This RFC defines no security machinery of its own. It points to the considerations in RFC 2779 for instant messaging in general, RFC 4975 and RFC 3261 for MSRP chat, RFC 6121 and RFC 6120 for XMPP, RFC 7247 for SIP-XMPP interworking, and RFC 7572 for end-to-end encryption of instant messages.

Internationalization is also handled by reference: relevant discussion of internationalized text in messages is in RFC 7572.
sections.eli5: This document does not add new locks. It tells you to look at the older documents that explain the locks.
